Lemon chickpea salad

Published 2026-09-16

Chickpeas, crunchy cucumber and tomatoes tossed in a lemon dressing, finished with feta and parsley. Drain the chickpeas well and pat wet cucumber dry to keep excess water out of the bowl.

Prep
~10 min
Method
No-cook
Total
~10 min
Ingredients & Method ↓

Development edition · Awaits kitchen testing.

Ingredients Method Storage

Ingredients

How many people?
2

Estimated to serve 2 people as a light meal.

  • For the salad
  • 240 g chickpeas, drained and rinsed
    About 1 standard 15 oz / 425 g can, drained.
    Missing this?

    Use cooked white beans, drained · 240 g

    White beans are softer and may break apart more easily. Milder flavor with a creamier mouthfeel. Fold gently so the beans keep their shape. Fold gently so the beans keep their shape. Use the same drained weight.

  • 1 cup (150 g) diced cucumber
  • 1 cup (150 g) cherry tomatoes, halved
  • ⅓ cup (50 g) crumbled feta
    Missing this?

    Use diced avocado · 50 g

    Soft and buttery rather than crumbly. No saltiness or tang — taste and adjust lemon and salt. Fold in at the end. Taste and adjust lemon and salt before serving. Fold in at the end. Taste and adjust lemon and salt. A suggested variation, not an equivalent cheese replacement.

  • ¼ cup chopped flat-leaf parsley, loosely packed
    Missing this?

    Use chopped dill, loosely packed · 2 tbsp

    Same texture — fine, leafy herb. Dill is more assertive and anise-forward than parsley. Add with the vegetables, then taste before adding more. Add with the vegetables, then taste before adding more. Start with half the parsley volume; add more to taste.

  • For the dressing
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 tbsp lemon juice, plus more to taste
  • Black pepper and salt, to taste

Contains milk (feta). Check ingredient labels.

Method

You'll need
Large mixing bowl · Sieve · Knife and board · Whisk or fork · Serving spoon

Prepare

01

Whisk the dressing

Whisk the olive oil and lemon juice in the mixing bowl. Add a few grinds of black pepper.

Look for: The mixture looks slightly cloudy and combined. Whisk again if it separates.

Extra tip

Wait until the salad is assembled before adding salt.

Assemble

02

Add the crunch

Drain the chickpeas thoroughly. Add them to the dressing with cucumber, tomatoes and parsley. Toss gently.

Look for: The ingredients look lightly coated, without a puddle of rinse water.

Extra tip

Pat wet cucumber dry with a clean cloth before adding it.

Finish

03

Finish gently

Fold in the feta, keeping some crumbles intact. Taste, adjust lemon and salt if needed, and divide into portions.

Look for: You can still see distinct pieces of feta among the vegetables.

Extra tip

Avoid vigorous stirring, which turns the feta into a creamy coating.

Serve with

Serve as a light meal, or add bread or a cooked grain for a more substantial plate. These extras are not included in the ingredient amounts.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I make this ahead of time?

Yes, with one adjustment. Prepare the vegetables, chickpeas and dressing separately and keep them in the fridge, then combine just before eating. If you dress it in advance, the cucumber releases water and the lemon loses its edge. Assembled, it is best within a few hours.

How long does it keep in the fridge?

Stored in an airtight container at or below 40°F (4°C), the assembled salad keeps for two to three days. The texture softens after the first day as the cucumber continues to release moisture. Drain off any liquid that collects and taste before adding more lemon or salt.

What can I use instead of feta?

Diced avocado works well, though it changes the character of the dish: it is buttery rather than salty and tangy, so you will want more lemon and salt to compensate. Fold it in at the very end. For a closer match in saltiness, a firm ricotta salata behaves similarly to feta.

Do I need to peel the cucumber?

No. The skin adds color and holds the pieces together as you toss. If you are using a thick-skinned field cucumber, the skin can taste bitter, so peeling is reasonable there. With English or Persian cucumbers, leave it on. If the seed center looks very watery, scoop some out before dicing.

One way to change it up

For a creamier version, use the avocado option above. The illustration shows the original feta version.

Storage & Prep ahead

For a crisper result, keep the dressing and feta separate from the prepared vegetables until serving. Refrigerate the components in covered containers.

Keep at 40°F (4°C) or colder. Refrigerate within 2 hours of preparation, or within 1 hour above 90°F (32°C). Discard if left out longer. Storage life depends on ingredient freshness and preparation.
